newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh lifts ban on bank credit against shares.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh lifts ban on bank credit against shares.

text.p: Bangladesh's central bank on Saturday lifted restrictions on bank credit against share certificates, bank officials said.
The restriction on bank credit was imposed early this month to cool down the overheated stock market.
The officials said the commercial banks had been allowed to resume lending from Saturday against shares and debentures.
Banks have been asked to sanction loans of up to a maximum 40 percent of the market value of shares and debentures of the listed companies.
The officials said the fresh move was taken after share investors reported a severe funding crisis, which triggered a sharp decline in stock prices.
The Dhaka Stock Exchange all-share index dropped to 3,033.36 on Thursday from 3,627.01 on November 16.
Daily turnover, which shot up to one billion taka earlier this month, slumped to 26.3 million on Thursday. Friday is the weekend in Moslem Bangladesh.
